title: $\mathrm{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$ is essentially small
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and let $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be defined
in a fixed universe. Then the isomorphism classes of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ form a set.
Here $\ell$ is a prime, $E$ is a finite subextension of a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the coefficient rings are the condensed rings of [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back as $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In particular these are not the discrete constant coefficient sheaves. The full category $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is that of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Sets and small site skeletons are taken in the larger universe $\mathcal V$ of [def-weil-size-convention], with the schemes and coefficient data in its fixed smaller bound $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$.

proof.text: Use the sectionwise presentation of the coefficient module objects, justified as follows. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], the tensor of abelian sheaves is the sheafification of the pointwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$. Thus an action $\Lambda_X\otimes M\to M$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is, by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and the defining universal property of the ordinary tensor product, precisely a natural family of bilinear maps $\Lambda_X(V)\times M(V)\to M(V)$. The unit and associativity diagrams are exactly $1m=m$ and $(ab)m=a(bm)$, checked on pure tensors; morphisms are exactly the sectionwise linear maps. This gives an equivalence, retaining the underlying abelian sheaf, with [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. We use it for the coefficient ring sheaf itself, without making that ring constant. Now use the bounded schemes and compatible small site skeletons of [def-weil-size-convention]. All sets below are $\mathcal V$-sets. The collection of $\mathcal U$-bounded schemes and their morphisms is a set in $\mathcal V$: their underlying spaces, rings, sheaf maps and structure maps are set-theoretic data in the set $\mathcal U$. Thus the finite lists of locally closed immersions into the fixed $X$ form a set, and the subcollection that are stratifications also forms a set [def-constructible-stratification]. The Noetherian scheme $X$ is quasi-compact by the stated convention and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Hence the qcqs clause of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] applies: every constructible $F$ admits one of these finite stratifications $a:S_a\to X$ on which its restrictions have finite constant local models. These models are finite free, as the following elementary calculation shows. Evaluation at the one-point profinite set in [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] gives the scalar field $R=\Lambda(*)=E$ or $\Qlb$; every element of $\Qlb$ lies in a finite subextension because it is algebraic. For each finitely presented scalar module $P$, its finite presentation [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], specialized to ordinary $R$-modules, supplies finitely many spanning vectors. Choose a maximal linearly independent sublist. For every omitted vector, maximality gives a dependence with the independent sublist; the coefficient on the omitted vector must be nonzero and can be divided out, expressing it in the span. This gives $P\cong R^r$ with $r\geq0$. The induced isomorphism $\Lambda_U\otimes_R P\cong\Lambda_U^r$ sends $b\otimes\sum_j c_je_j$ to $(bc_j)_j$ and has inverse $(b_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j$. The balanced bilinear relations make these maps well defined and inverse; these formulas first define maps on the constant models and then extend to their sheafifications by the universal property already cited. Thus $a^*F$ is lisse. Clause (2) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] also preserves this property on every refinement. Here and below lisse means pro-etale locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of the coefficient ring sheaf. We shall bound the possible lisse restrictions by descent data, and then bound the additional gluing between strata.

source.place: First paragraph, choice of an adapted finite stratification; second paragraph, set of finite stratifications

proof.text: We first identify inverse image along a site object with slice restriction, including for the present nonconstant coefficient rings. If $u:U\to S$ is an object of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $S_{\mathrm{proét}}/U$. For an object $T\to U$, an index $(V,T\to U\times_S V)$ in the inverse-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is equivalently an $S$-map $T\to V$. The index $(T,\mathrm{id}_T)$ is initial in this category, hence terminal in the opposite indexing category of that formula. The presheaf inverse image at $T$ is consequently $M(T)$, with the original restriction maps. This is already a sheaf because coverings in the slice are the original coverings, so sheafification does nothing. The same calculation applies to the coefficient ring and its action. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], $u^*$ on coefficient modules is this inverse image and $u^{-1}\Lambda_S\simeq\Lambda_U$. Therefore a trivialization $u^*L\simeq\Lambda_U^r$ identifies $L(T)$ with $\Lambda_S(T)^r$ naturally for every $T\to U$.

source.place: Section 00XZ (localization), inverse-image formula; site identification uses more-morphisms.tex Tags 094T/0951 through the cited localization node

proof.text: Fix a stratum $S$ and a lisse $L$. On the chosen small skeleton choose a trivializing covering $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ and integers $r_i\geq0$. Remove repetitions of the same site object, choosing one trivialization for each remaining object; repetitions do not affect the covering condition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus $I$ can be a subset of the set of site objects. There is no need to make the covering finite. On $U_{ij}=U_i\times_SU_j$, the two trivializations differ by mutually inverse matrices $g_{ij}$ and $g_{ij}^{-1}$, of sizes $r_j\times r_i$ and $r_i\times r_j$, with entries in $\Lambda_S(U_{ij})$. Write $g_{ij}$ in the direction from the $i$-coordinates to the $j$-coordinates. On $U_i\times_SU_j\times_SU_k$ the cocycle equation is $p_{jk}^*g_{jk}\,p_{ij}^*g_{ij}=p_{ik}^*g_{ik}$. On the diagonal $\delta_i:U_i\to U_i\times_SU_i$ it is $\delta_i^*g_{ii}=I_{r_i}$. No equation $g_{ii}=I$ on the entire self-overlap is imposed: the two projections of a non-monomorphic cover can give different trivializations there. Indeed a module-sheaf map between finite free modules is determined by the images of its standard basis sections; naturality and linearity give the same matrix on every test object [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Different ranks are allowed, including empty overlaps. All these codes form a set: take subsets $I$ of the fixed object set, functions $I\to\mathbf N$, and products of the matrix-entry sets over pairs of indices, then impose the equations by separation. All coefficient section sets and index sets lie in $\mathcal V$.

source.place: First paragraph, transition data; arbitrary small covers in place of the unnecessary finite quasi-compact refinement

proof.text: A code gives an explicit model rather than requiring a choice from a class of sheaves. For $V\in S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ put $L_c(V)$ equal to the families $s_i\in\Lambda_S(V\times_SU_i)^{r_i}$ such that $s_j=g_{ij}s_i$ on $V\times_SU_i\times_SU_j$, with restrictions componentwise and the $\Lambda_S(V)$-action induced by restriction. This is a sheaf: along any covering of $V$, each component glues uniquely by the coefficient sheaf axiom, and each matrix equality holds after gluing because it holds on that covering. This is exactly the equalizer sheaf condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], applied componentwise; base change of coverings is part of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. If $L$ produces the code $c$, the isomorphisms of step 2 and the sheaf axiom for the covering $\{V\times_SU_i\to V\}$ identify $L(V)$ with $L_c(V)$: a section gives its compatible tuple, and conversely the tuple glues to a unique section. These identifications respect restrictions, addition and scalar multiplication [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence $L\simeq L_c$, and the set of codes provides a set of actual sheaves containing an isomorphic copy of every lisse restriction. For an empty stratum the same equalizer is the zero module sheaf.

source.place: Tags 00VM/00VR, definition-sheaf-sets/definition-sheaf; direct equalizer construction, also the gluing-of-maps argument of Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps

proof.text: Fix a finite stratification and one model $L_a$ on each $S_a$. Put $H=\prod_a a_*L_a$, a fixed $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf. This finite product is computed sectionwise: componentwise gluing verifies the sheaf axiom, with componentwise ring action. The functors and adjunctions $a^*\dashv a_*$ exist for these condensed coefficients by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Given $F$ and isomorphisms $\alpha_a:a^*F\simeq L_a$, let $t:F\to H$ have components $a_*\alpha_a\circ\eta_a(F)$. We claim $t$ is monic. Let $k:K\to F$ be its kernel, which is sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The equation $t_a k=0$ implies $\eta_a(F)k=0$, since $a_*\alpha_a$ is invertible. Apply the exact functor $a^*$ of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] and compose with the adjunction counit. The triangle identity $\varepsilon_{a,a^*F}\circ a^*\eta_a(F)=1_{a^*F}$ gives $a^*k=0$. Exactness also makes $a^*k$ monic, so $a^*K=0$ for every stratum. Clause (3) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] detects exactness on the strata; applied to $0\to K\to0$, it gives $K=0$. Thus $F$ is isomorphic to a subsheaf of $H$. This argument does not require strata to factor through one another or any chosen reduced complement.

source.place: First paragraph, additional gluing between strata: explicit encoding by a subsheaf of the product of the stratum pushforwards, using exact stratum detection

proof.text: For each fixed $H$, its subsheaves form a set. A monomorphism $N\to H$ is injective on sections because kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; identify $N$ with its sectionwise images. Such a subsheaf is determined by the family of subsets $N(V)\subseteq H(V)$, one for each object of the fixed small site, since its operations and restrictions are inherited from $H$. These families lie in the set $\prod_V\mathcal P(H(V))$; imposing module, restriction, and sheaf conditions selects a subset. Therefore subsheaves of $H$ supply a set of representatives containing, up to isomorphism, all the $F$ of step 5. Finally take the union over the set of finite stratifications from step 1 and, for each, over the finite products of sets of codes from steps 3--4. This is a set in $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention] containing a representative of every constructible sheaf. Retain the representatives that are constructible and quotient this set by isomorphism; the result is precisely the asserted set of isomorphism classes. Rank zero and empty strata cause no exception; when $X$ is empty, the empty-stratum detection of step 5 gives $F=0$.

source.place: Second paragraph, set of all data and isomorphism classes; explicit power-set bound for the additional gluing data

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; descent reconstructed by the sheaf equalizer, with gluing between strata encoded by subsheaves rather than an unproved Ext-size assertion

split_report.summary: Six-step split with no new nodes. Checked the project Lean and all cited statements. Made the coefficient and universe conventions explicit, built lisse models from small covering/matrix codes by the sheaf equalizer, and encoded cross-stratum gluing as subsheaves of a fixed finite product of pushforwards. Exact pullback, adjunction triangles and existing stratum detection prove the required embedding. Rectangular transition matrices and arbitrary small covers avoid unnecessary common-rank and finite-refinement assumptions. No Lean written or compiled. Independent second reading supplied the finite-basis and scalar-tensor calculation and the precise cocycle/diagonal equations for non-monomorphic covers.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes unit sk-lem-coefficient-heart proof (2): finite adapted stratifications (step 1), finite-rank descent data on a covering (steps 2--4), and set of global data (steps 5--6). Within the detail node, the uncited Ext-set sentence is replaced by an explicit subsheaf encoding of the same cross-stratum gluing; the unit route is unchanged.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-a3ae6d83a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement matches the main-20261015 blueprint det-lem-coefficient-heart-small.md word for word (Noetherian X, Lambda=E or Qlb, fixed universe, a set of isomorphism classes); the added conventions only spell out existing meanings and weaken nothing. There are no new nodes. The duplicate scan found only the unit sk-lem-coefficient-heart (clause 2) and its citers. The dependency closure (2338 nodes) does not contain the item, so there is no cycle. Steps 1-4 and 6 follow unit step (2): stratification, then descent codes, then a set. Step 5 replaces the blueprint's unsupported Ext^1 sentence with a sound embedding F into the product of a_*L_a. Step 1: Noetherian gives qcqs (Mathlib leaf 01OY), so sk-def-sfb-constructible clause (2) applies; Lambda(*) is E or Qlb (a field), so finitely presented modules are free and the local models are Lambda^r. A stratification using schemes outside the bound can be replaced by an isomorphic one inside it; this is implicit and takes one line. Step 2: (T,can) is initial in I_T, so the colimit over I_T^op is M(T); with localization clause (1) and cartesian-coefficients this gives L(T)=Lambda_S(T)^r for the condensed coefficients themselves. Step 3: codes use rectangular inverse matrices, the triple cocycle and the diagonal normalization; rank 0, empty overlaps and non-monomorphic covers are handled. Step 4: L_c is a sheaf for every code by the 00VM/00VR equalizer, and L is isomorphic to L_c for a code coming from L; no effective-descent theorem is used, and step 6 filters by constructibility. Step 5: the triangle identity gives a^*k=0; exactness of a^* (cartesian-coefficients) and common-stratification (3) give K=0. Step 6: subobjects inject into the product over V of P(H(V)), which is a V-set. Stacks tags 00XZ, 00VM, 00VR, 04TQ, 094T, 0951 and 01OY all resolve to the cited labels. All three kinds of Mathlib search are recorded, with no match. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization (clause 1, slice-site identification) and sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients (coefficient inverse image and exact module pullback); both are generic and replace no unit step. No changes.
